scope: Proposition 6.4 (Preservation of the invariant) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that all nonempty parents at stage r have base dimension at least two and satisfy (6.4)–(6.6). At r = 0 use the compact radial blocks of Theorem 6.1; at r ≥ 1 suppose also that the packet geometry and Theorem 6.2 hold. Processing label r produces the compatible smooth split, preserves the forced signs, and gives the same assertions at stage r + 1. Exactly 399 new warp factors, with common indices, are appended at this stage. Each whole resulting packet has a finite relevant old warp list.
